items.title: Focus Question: What role do magnetic forces play in the everyday technology of a hybrid car and a phone?

answer.html: Magnetic forces on currents turn the electric motors that drive a hybrid car's wheels and its cooling fans, make a phone's speaker and vibration motor move, and, through sensors, help a phone's compass work. In each case a magnetic field exerts a force on moving charge in a wire.

items.title: Predict (Figure 14 margin): A wire carries current in a magnetic field and feels a force. What would happen to the force if the direction of the field were reversed? What if both the current and the field were reversed?

question.html: Physics idea The force direction comes from the right-hand rule using the field and the current, and its size is 𝐼𝐿𝐵sin𝜃. Work Reversing only the field reverses the palm direction, so the force reverses. Reversing both flips the force twice, which returns it to the original direction. The size of the force stays the same in all cases.

answer.html: Reversing only the field reverses the force. Reversing both the current and the field leaves the force direction unchanged. The magnitude is the same in both cases.

items.title: Revisit the Encounter the Phenomenon Question (Lesson 2 Investigate): A student wants to explain how the motor in an electric bicycle turns its wheel. What information from this lesson helps?

answer.html: A current in a wire in a magnetic field feels a force 𝐹= 𝐼𝐿𝐵sin𝜃. In the motor's coil, the current flows in opposite directions on opposite sides, so the forces are opposite and make a torque. A commutator reverses the current each half turn so the torque keeps the same direction, and the coil keeps turning and drives the wheel. Using electromagnets with many loops and large currents makes the forces large.

items.title: Virtual Investigation: Charge in a Magnetic Field (online)

question.html: This activity needs the online simulation and cannot be run from the book. The expected result, from 𝐹= 𝑞𝑣𝐵sin𝜃, is stated here as a representative outcome rather than measured data. Suppose the simulation launches an electron so that its velocity makes an angle of 30° with a uniform field.

answer.html: Only the component of velocity perpendicular to the field produces a force, and that force is perpendicular to both the velocity and the field. The electron moves in a circle around the field direction while the component of its velocity along the field is unchanged, so its path is a spiral (helix). The electron's speed does not change, because the magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity. Making the electron a proton reverses the sense of the circling.

items.title: Explain (Figure 17 margin): A coil of wire in a galvanometer sits between magnet poles. Why does the coil rotate when current is sent through it, and why does it turn only a limited angle?

question.html: Physics idea The force on a current in a magnetic field follows the right-hand rule, and forces on the opposite sides of the coil make a torque. A spring in the meter provides a restoring torque. Work Current goes one way along one side of the coil and the opposite way along the other side. The field pushes one side up and the other down, which gives a torque. The turned coil twists a spring, whose restoring torque grows with the angle until it equals the magnetic torque.

answer.html: The field exerts equal and opposite forces on the two sides of the coil, producing a torque. The coil turns until the torque of the spring balances the magnetic torque, so the angle is proportional to the current.

answer.html: A cordless drill, a bench grinder, a garage-door opener, or an air compressor. Each has an electric motor that converts electrical energy into the rotational mechanical energy of a shaft.

items.title: Practice Problems (Lesson 2, Problems 19–24) Problem 19 (Lesson 2 Practice): A student says the direction of the force on a wire in a field can be found from the current direction alone. Correct the student, then find the direction of the force on a wire carrying current east in a field that points straight down.

question.html: What we know / need to find Current east, field down. Find the force direction, and say what must be known. Physics idea Right-hand rule: fingers along the field, thumb along the conventional current, palm faces the force. The force depends on both directions. Work Point the fingers down. To point the thumb east, the palm must face north. So the force is north. The direction would change if either the field or the current were different, so both must be known.

answer.html: You must know both the direction of the field and the direction of the conventional current. For current east and a downward field, the force is toward the north.

Problem 24 (Lesson 2 Practice, Challenge): For a homemade earphone, a coil of 30 loops, 2.0 cm in diameter, is glued to the bottom of a paper cup and connected to a music player. A magnet supplies the field. (a) How should the field be oriented to make the cup vibrate? (b) If the field at the wire is 0.15 T and the current is 0.50 A, what is the force on the coil?

question.html: What we know / need to find 𝑁= 30 loops, 𝑑= 2.0 cm, 𝐵= 0.15 T, 𝐼= 0.50 A. Find the orientation of the field and the force. Physics idea The force on the wire is perpendicular to both the current and the field. The current runs around the circle. For the cup to vibrate, the coil must be pushed along its axis, in and out of the cup bottom. The force is 𝐹= 𝐼𝐿𝐵 for a wire perpendicular to the field. Work (a) If the field pointed along the axis, the force on the wire would be in the plane of the coil, pushing the coil outward or inward and not moving the cup. If the field at the wire is radial (perpendicular to both the wire and the axis), the force is along the axis. A bar magnet with one pole at the center of the coil, aligned with the coil's axis, gives a nearly radial field. The alternating current from the player reverses the force, so the cup moves in and out at the frequency of the sound. Work (b) The total length of wire in the field is 𝐿= 𝑁𝜋𝑑= (30)𝜋(0.020 m) = 1.9 m. Then 𝐹= 𝐼𝐿𝐵= (0.50 A)(1.9 m)(0.15 T) = 0.14 N.

answer.html: (a) Put one pole of the magnet at the center of the coil along its axis so the field at the wire is radial, and the force is along the axis. (b) 𝐹= 0.14 N

items.title: Check Your Progress and Practice for Charged Particles (Lesson 2, Problems 25–37) Problem 25 (Lesson 2 Practice): What is the direction of the force on an electron moving west in a magnetic field that points north?

question.html: What we know / need to find 𝑣 is west, 𝐵 is north, charge is negative. Find the force direction. Physics idea The right-hand rule for a positive charge gives the force direction, and the force on a negative charge is opposite. Work For a positive charge: fingers north (the field), thumb west (the velocity); the palm faces down. So the force on a positive charge would be down, and the force on an electron is the opposite.

answer.html: Upward (away from the ground).

items.title: Check The force is perpendicular to both west and north, so it must be vertical. Problem 26 (Lesson 2 Practice): Find the magnitude and direction of the force on a proton moving to the left at 2.5 × 107 m/s through a 0.6-T field directed into the page

For the direction, put the fingers into the page and the thumb to the left: the palm faces down the page.

Problem 31 (Check Your Progress): Explain how the commutator helps a motor in a cordless drill turn, and what would happen if it were replaced by two solid slip rings that keep the current in the coil in the same direction

answer.html: The coil in a motor feels forces that are opposite on its two sides, giving a torque. Half a turn later, the sides have swapped places, so with the same current the torque would reverse and pull the coil back. A split-ring commutator reverses the current every half turn, so the torque keeps the same sense and the coil spins continuously, converting electrical energy to rotational mechanical energy. With solid slip rings the current direction would never reverse, so the coil would swing past the vertical position, be pulled back, and rock back and forth until it stopped near the vertical position instead of spinning.

items.title: 32 (Check Your Progress): Find the direction of the force on an east-west wire with the current flowing west, in Earth's field, which is taken to point north and to be perpendicular to the wire

question.html: What we know / need to find The wire runs east-west with the current to the west. The field points north. Find the force direction. Physics idea Right-hand rule: fingers along the field, thumb along the current, palm faces the force. Work Point the fingers north. To point the thumb west, the right hand must be palm down. The palm faces down.

answer.html: Downward (toward the ground).

items.title: Check The force is perpendicular to both west and north, so it is vertical. Problem 33(a) (Check Your Progress): Electrons circulate clockwise in a ring, as seen from above. What directions must the magnetic and electric fields have?

question.html: What we know / need to find Electrons move clockwise, seen from above. Find the directions of 𝐵 and 𝐸. Physics idea The magnetic force supplies the inward (centripetal) force and is perpendicular to 𝑣. The electric force must speed the electrons up, so it must point along their velocity. The force on a negative charge is opposite to 𝐸. Work Take the electron at the top of the circle, moving to the right. The force must point down, toward the center. A positive charge would be pushed the opposite way, up. With the thumb to the right and the palm facing up, the fingers point into the page (away from the viewer). So 𝐵 is into the page. The electric force must be tangent and clockwise, so 𝐸 must point the opposite way, tangent and counterclockwise.

answer.html: The magnetic field points perpendicular to the plane of the ring, away from the viewer (down, into the page, when seen from above). The electric field points tangent to the ring in the counterclockwise direction, opposite to the electrons' motion.

items.title: 33(b) (Check Your Progress): The electrons are now made to circulate counterclockwise instead. Which field directions must be changed?

question.html: Physics idea Reversing the direction of motion reverses the magnetic force for the same field, so 𝐵 must be reversed to keep the force pointing inward. The electric force must still speed the electrons up. Work At the top of the ring the electron now moves to the left. The inward force is down, so a positive charge would be pushed up. With the thumb left and the palm up, the fingers point out of the page, so 𝐵 must point out of the page, toward the viewer. For 𝐸, the electrons must speed up in the counterclockwise direction, and the force on a negative charge is opposite to 𝐸, so 𝐸 must point clockwise.

answer.html: Both fields must be reversed. The magnetic field now points up, toward the viewer (out of the page, seen from above), and the electric field is tangent in the clockwise direction.

items.title: 34 (Check Your Progress): Compare a galvanometer with a loudspeaker. How are they similar and different?

answer.html: Similar: both have a coil of wire in a magnetic field, and a current in the coil makes a force from the field that moves the coil, and a spring or elastic mount pushes the coil back toward its rest position. Different: in a galvanometer the coil turns through a limited angle that is proportional to a steady current, and a needle shows the reading. In a loudspeaker the coil sits in a radial field and moves in and out along its axis, pushing the cone, and it moves back and forth at the frequency of the alternating current, producing sound.

items.title: 35 (Check Your Progress): The plane of a motor's armature coil is perpendicular to the field, where the torque is zero. A student says that if the motor starts in this position, it will not start. Is the student right? How do real motors solve the problem?

question.html: Physics idea At the zero-torque position there is no net torque, so a coil that is not already turning would not begin to turn. A spinning coil, though, carries on through by inertia. Work If the coil starts exactly at that position with no current torque, the student is right: nothing would start it turning. Real motors use several coils at different angles to the field, so when one coil has zero torque the others are not in that position and the armature always has a net torque. A spinning motor also passes through the position because of its rotational inertia.

answer.html: The student is right for a single coil starting exactly in that position. Real motors have several coils set at different angles, so the motor always has some torque, and once spinning, inertia carries the armature past the zero-torque position.

items.title: Check A voltmeter should have a large resistance so that it draws little current from the circuit. Problem 37 (Check Your Progress, Critical Thinking): Two parallel current-carrying wires move apart from each other. Compare the directions of the currents.

question.html: Physics idea Each wire is in the field of the other, and the force on a current in a field follows the right-hand rule. Work Take wire 1 with current out of the page (toward you), and wire 2 to its right. The field of wire 1 circulates counterclockwise, so at wire 2 it points up the page. Suppose the current in wire 2 is into the page. With the fingers pointing up the page and the thumb into the page, the palm faces right, away from wire 1. So the wires are pushed apart. If the current were out of the page, the force would be to the left, toward wire 1.

answer.html: The currents are in opposite directions. (Wires with currents in the same direction would attract.)

items.title: 3D Thinking (Ask Questions to Clarify): Write three questions about how a hospital MRI scanner uses magnets to image the inside of the body

question.html: This is an open-ended research prompt; sample questions and short answers follow.

answer.html: 1. Why does an MRI machine need such a strong magnet? The scanner uses a large solenoid carrying a big current, often cooled so its wire has almost no resistance, to produce a field of 1.5 T or more. A strong field lines up many of the protons in the body's atoms, so the signal is large enough to detect. 2. Why do patients have to remove metal objects? A strong field magnetizes ferromagnetic objects and pulls on them, so loose steel items could fly toward the magnet. 3. How is the image made without cutting the body? After the protons are lined up, radio pulses disturb them, and as they return to alignment they give off signals whose timing depends on the kind of tissue. A computer uses these signals to build a map of the tissues.

Work (i) From 𝑟= 3.0 cm to 6.0 cm the field went from 52 𝜇T to 27 𝜇T, a decrease by a factor of 1.9. From 5.0 cm to 10.0 cm it went from 32 𝜇T to 16 𝜇T, a factor of 2.0. Both are close to 2. question.html: This is a project step: revisit your own STEM unit project and summarize the evidence from this module. Suppose a project is to design an electromagnetic lifting device for a school robotics contest. Sample (not a unique) answer:

answer.html: Evidence from this module that supports the design: the field of the coil grows with the current, the number of loops, and how close they are packed; an iron core greatly increases the field; the device can be switched off by cutting the current, so the load can be released on command; and a magnetic force on a current is 𝐹= 𝐼𝐿𝐵sin𝜃, so a larger current gives a larger force. items.title: Lesson 1 Investigate: Applying Practices: Modeling Magnetic Fields (online)

question.html: This is an online/hands-on activity whose data and instructions are not available here, so no values can be solved. Suppose the model has you sketch the field of a current loop and of a bar magnet.

answer.html: The field lines of a bar magnet run outside from the north pole to the south pole and close through the magnet. A current loop has lines that pass through the loop in one direction (given by the right-hand rule) and return around the outside, so it looks like a short bar magnet. The lines bunch up where the field is strong (at the magnet's poles and inside the loop) and spread out where it is weak.

items.title: Focus Question: What role do magnetic forces play in everyday life?

answer.html: Magnetic forces on currents and moving charges drive electric motors (fans, drones, appliances), make loudspeakers, headphones, and earbuds produce sound, move the needles in galvanometers and meters, and steer charged particle beams in accelerators such as synchrotrons.

items.title: Predict (Figure 14 margin): What would happen to the force if the current changed direction?

question.html: Since the force direction is set by the right-hand rule with the current and the field, reversing the current reverses the force (the palm faces the opposite way) while its magnitude stays 𝐼𝐿𝐵.

answer.html: The force would reverse direction (same magnitude).

items.title: Revisit the Encounter the Phenomenon Question (Lesson 2 Investigate): What information from this lesson helps answer the Unit and Module questions?

answer.html: The lesson shows that magnetic fields act on moving charges and currents, with force 𝐹= 𝐼𝐿𝐵sin𝜃 on a wire and 𝐹= 𝑞𝑣𝐵sin𝜃 on a moving charge. In an electromagnet the field itself comes from current, so increasing the current and the number of loops increases the field and the forces on other magnets and on ferromagnetic objects. The module-level answer (large current, many loops, iron core) is in the CER answer above.

items.title: Virtual Investigation: Charge in a Magnetic Field (online)

question.html: This activity needs the online simulation and cannot be run from the book. The expected result, from 𝐹= 𝑞𝑣𝐵sin𝜃, is stated here as a representative outcome rather than measured data.

answer.html: A moving charged particle feels a force perpendicular to both its velocity and the field, so it moves along a curve (a circle if the velocity is perpendicular to the field). Reversing the sign of the charge or the field direction reverses the bend. A particle moving parallel to the field feels no force and goes straight. The speed of the particle does not change, because the force is always perpendicular to the velocity.

items.title: Explain (Figure 17 margin): What causes the wire loop to rotate?

question.html: Current goes in one side of the loop and out the other, so it flows in opposite directions along the two sides that cross the field. By the right-hand rule, the field then pushes one side up and the other side down.

answer.html: The magnetic field exerts forces in opposite directions on the two sides of the loop (current flows opposite ways along them), and these equal and opposite forces form a torque that rotates the loop.

items.title: Get It? (p. 560): Compare how you would use a resistor to convert a galvanometer first to an ammeter and then to a voltmeter

answer.html: Ammeter: connect a small-resistance shunt resistor in parallel with the galvanometer, so most of the current bypasses the meter and only a small known fraction goes through it. Voltmeter: connect a large-resistance multiplier resistor in series with the galvanometer, so that the full-scale current flows through the meter when the desired voltage is applied across the combination.

items.title: Get It? (p. 560): Describe an object at home that uses an electric motor

answer.html: A washing machine, a blender, a fan, a vacuum cleaner, or a hair dryer: each has an electric motor that turns electrical energy into rotational mechanical energy.

items.title: Get It? (p. 562): Describe a real-life situation in which you would want to calculate the force of a magnetic field on a moving charged particle

answer.html: Designing the magnets that bend a proton beam in a particle accelerator (such as the LHC) or a cathode-ray tube, or estimating the force on charged particles in Earth's magnetic field, as in the aurora. Each needs 𝐹= 𝑞𝑣𝐵sin𝜃.

items.title: 24 (Lesson 2 Practice, Challenge) Homemade loudspeaker: how should the magnetic field be oriented to make the plate vibrate?

question.html: What we know / need to find A round coil (1 cm diameter, 20 loops) is glued to an aluminum pie plate and connected to the music player; a bar magnet supplies the field. Find the orientation of the field. Physics idea The force on the wire is perpendicular to both the current and the field. The current in the coil runs around the circle (tangent to the coil). For the plate to vibrate, the coil must be pushed along its own axis (in and out of the plate's surface), like the cone of a loudspeaker. Work The force is along the coil's axis when the field at every point of the coil is perpendicular to the wire and points radially (toward or away from the axis, in the plane of the coil). If the field were along the axis, the force on the coil would be in the plane of the loops (outward or inward on the coil), which would only squeeze or stretch the coil and not move the plate. A bar magnet can give a nearly radial field if one pole is placed at the center of the coil with the magnet's axis along the coil's axis, because the field lines spread out from the pole. The alternating current from the player then reverses the force, so the coil and plate move in and out at the frequency of the sound.

answer.html: Put one pole of the bar magnet at the center of the coil, with the magnet along the coil's axis (perpendicular to the plate), so the field through the wire is radial (perpendicular to the wire and the plate's axis). The force on the coil is then along the axis and the plate vibrates with the current.

items.title: Check The field is of the same order as in Problem 27, as expected for similar charges and speeds. Problem 31 (Check Your Progress) Explain how electric motors use magnets to convert electrical energy to mechanical energy.

answer.html: A motor has a coil of wire (the armature) on an axle between magnet poles. When current flows in the coil, the magnetic field exerts forces on the wires that are opposite on the two sides of the coil, producing a torque that turns the coil. A split-ring commutator reverses the current every half turn, so the torque keeps the coil turning in the same direction. The electrical energy supplied by the current is converted into the rotational (mechanical) energy of the armature.

items.title: 32 (Check Your Progress) Force on an east-west wire with current east, perpendicular to Earth's magnetic field

question.html: What we know / need to find The wire runs east-west with the current to the east. Earth's magnetic field is taken to point north and to be perpendicular to the wire. Find the direction of the force. Physics idea Right-hand rule for the force on a current: fingers along the field, thumb along the current, palm faces the force. Work Point the fingers north. To point the thumb east, the right hand must be palm up. The palm faces up.

answer.html: Upward (away from the ground).

items.title: Check The force is perpendicular to both east and north, so it is vertical. Problem 33(a) (Check Your Progress) Protons circulating clockwise: what direction must the magnetic and electric fields be?

question.html: What we know / need to find Protons move clockwise in a circle, seen from above. Find the directions of 𝐵 and 𝐸. Physics idea The magnetic force supplies the inward (centripetal) force, and it is perpendicular to 𝑣. The electric force must speed the protons up, so it must point along their velocity (the force on a positive charge is in the direction of 𝐸). Work Take the proton at the top of the circle, moving to the right. The force must point down, toward the center. Using the right-hand rule, with the thumb to the right and the palm facing down, the fingers point out of the page (toward the viewer). Check: for a proton moving to the right and a field out of the page, the force is down. At any other point of the circle the same field out of the page gives a force toward the center. The electric field must point along the direction of motion at each point, tangent to the circle in the clockwise sense.

answer.html: The magnetic field points perpendicular to the plane of the circle, toward the viewer (out of the page, when the circle is seen from above). The electric fields point tangent to the circle in the clockwise direction, the same way the protons move.

items.title: Check If the field were reversed, the protons would be pushed outward and leave the circle. Problem 33(b) (Check Your Progress) Antiprotons circulating counterclockwise: must the field directions be changed?

question.html: Physics idea Antiprotons have negative charge, so for the same field the force is opposite to the force on protons. The electric force on a negative charge is opposite to 𝐸. Work Magnetic field: an antiproton at the top of the circle now moves to the left. The right-hand rule for a positive charge, with 𝐵 out of the page and the velocity to the left, gives a force up (away from the center). The antiproton has negative charge, so the actual force is down, toward the center. So 𝐵 out of the page works with no change. Electric field: the antiprotons must speed up in the counterclockwise direction, but the force on them is opposite to 𝐸, so 𝐸 must point clockwise, which is the same direction as for protons.

answer.html: No change is needed for either field. The magnetic field stays pointing out of the page, and the electric fields stay tangent in the clockwise direction. (Reversing both the direction of motion and the sign of the charge cancels in both cases.)

items.title: 34 (Check Your Progress) Compare the galvanometer (Figure 17, right) and the electric motor (Figure 19). How are they similar and different?

answer.html: Similar: both have a coil of wire in a magnetic field; current in the coil causes forces on opposite sides of the coil in opposite directions, creating a torque that turns the coil. Different: in a galvanometer a small spring opposes the rotation, so the coil turns only a limited angle that is proportional to the current (used to measure current), and there is no commutator. In a motor there is no restoring spring and a split-ring commutator reverses the current every half turn, so the armature rotates continuously to do mechanical work.

items.title: 35 (Check Your Progress) When the armature plane is perpendicular to the field, there is no torque. Does this mean the coil does not rotate?

question.html: Physics idea Inertia: a rotating object keeps rotating unless a torque stops it. Work At that position the torque is momentarily zero, but the coil is already spinning, so its rotational inertia carries it past this position. The commutator then reverses the current, so the torque pushes it onward in the same direction instead of pulling it back.

answer.html: No. The coil keeps turning because of its angular momentum (inertia), and the commutator reverses the current as it passes this position, so the torque continues to push it in the same direction.

items.title: Check A voltmeter should have a large resistance so that it draws little current from the circuit. Problem 37 (Check Your Progress, Critical Thinking) Two parallel current-carrying wires move toward each other. Compare the currents' directions.

question.html: Physics idea Each wire is in the field of the other, and the force on a current in a field follows the right-hand rule. Work Take wire 1 with current out of the page (toward you), and wire 2 to its right with the same current direction. By the right-hand rule, the field of wire 1 at the location of wire 2 points up the page (the field circulates counterclockwise around a current toward you). For wire 2, with the fingers up the page and the thumb out of the page, the palm faces left, toward wire 1. So the wires are pulled together. If the currents were opposite, the force on wire 2 would be to the right, away from wire 1.

answer.html: The currents are in the same direction. (Wires with opposite currents would repel.)

items.title: 3D Thinking (Ask Questions to Clarify): Write three questions about XRF and how it was used to reveal Degas' hidden painting

question.html: This is an open-ended research prompt; sample questions and short answers based on the article follow.

answer.html: 1. How does XRF identify elements? A beam of radiation excites atoms so that they emit X-ray photons, and each element emits photons with its own characteristic wavelengths, so the wavelengths identify the elements present. 2. Why was a synchrotron needed? A synchrotron produces a very intense, narrow X-ray beam, which gives the high-resolution scans needed to map elements in tiny details of the paint (see Lesson 2: magnets bend the charged particles in the ring). 3. How did element maps show the hidden face? Each map shows where one element (such as iron or mercury) lies in the paint layers; layering maps of the pigment-related elements reveals the colors and shapes of the paint underneath, without damaging the top painting.

items.title: Data Analysis Lab 1: Plot the force as a function of distance

question.html: Plotted below (left: force vs. separation, with the curve an inverse-square law would give through the first point; right: the same data on log-log axes).

items.title: Data Analysis Lab 2: Claim. Does this force follow an inverse square law?

answer.html: No. The force falls off much faster than an inverse square law.

items.title: Data Analysis Lab 3: Evidence and Reasoning. Defend your claim using your graph.

question.html: Physics idea If 𝐹∝1 / 𝑑<sup>2</sup>, then (i) doubling the distance should cut the force to one quarter, and (ii) the product 𝐹𝑑<sup>2</sup> should be constant, and (iii) a log-log graph should be a straight line with slope −2. Work (i) From 𝑑= 1.0 cm to 2.0 cm the force changed from 3.93 N to 0.018 N, a decrease by a factor 3.93 / 0.018 ≈220, not 4. From 1.4 cm to 2.8 cm the force fell from 0.13 N to 0.0038 N, a factor of about 34, still much larger than 4. (ii) 𝐹𝑑<sup>2</sup> is not constant: it is 3.93 at 1.0 cm, 0.58 at 1.2 cm, 0.25 at 1.4 cm, 0.072 at 2.0 cm, and 0.025 at 3.0 cm (units N · cm<sup>2</sup>), a drop by a factor of roughly 150. (iii) The log-log plot is not a straight line of slope −2; the slope between neighboring points is about −12 at the smallest distances and then about −4 to −5 for separations above 2 cm, and a straight-line fit through all the points has a slope of about −6. A force law with slope between −4 and −6 falls much faster than 1 / 𝑑<sup>2</sup>. (For bar magnets, whose fields are dipole-like, the force at larger separation is expected to fall roughly as 1 / 𝑑<sup>4</sup>, which is consistent with the slope near −4 to −5 at larger separations. The steeper drop at the smallest separations comes from the magnets being too close to be treated as small dipoles; this explanation is a physical interpretation, not something the data alone prove.)

answer.html: The force does not follow an inverse square law: doubling the distance cut the force by a factor of about 30 to 200 instead of 4, 𝐹𝑑<sup>2</sup> is not constant, and the log-log graph has a slope between about −4 and −6 rather than −2.
